title: Libby accessibility-screener row
description: One row per unique intervention surfaced by clinician / researcher / trial_screener, describing how a patient could practically access it: standard-of-care, off-label use, clinical-trial, compassionate / expanded-access, or unavailable. Includes trial recruitment contacts and manufacturer medical-information lines so the user (or treating team) has actionable points of contact.

intervention_id.description: Matches the intervention_id used in clinical_evidence.jsonl / preclinical_evidence.jsonl / recommendations.jsonl.

modality.description: Therapeutic modality (BiTE / trispecific / ADC / radioligand / CAR-T / CAR-NK / small molecule / monoclonal antibody / vaccine / other). Reuse the value from trials.jsonl when one exists.

aliases.description: Every known identifier — generic INN/USAN, pharma code, dev-program code, nicknames. Mirrored from trials.jsonl when available.

access_status.description: How a patient could practically access the therapy today. **A single intervention can carry multiple access paths simultaneously.** `standard_of_care` = on-label for the patient's indication; `off_label_use` = approved (in any indication) and the patient's clinician could prescribe it off-label for the case's tumor type; `clinical_trial_only` = investigational, only via enrollment; `compassionate_use` / `expanded_access_program` = pre-approval extended access pathways; `unavailable` = no current access path; `not_yet_accessible` = approved/active elsewhere but the patient cannot currently reach it for logistics or geography. **Approval rule:** any FDA/EMA-approved drug carries `off_label_use` (because a clinician can prescribe it off-label for an unrelated tumor type) — and if active trials also exist, both `off_label_use` AND `clinical_trial_only` appear in this list. Order the array by actionability so the most patient-relevant path appears first.

regulatory_status.description: Approval state: 'FDA-approved (ES-SCLC, accelerated 2024)', 'FDA Fast Track (ES-SCLC)', 'EMA-approved', 'Breakthrough therapy designation', 'IND-cleared, no approval', 'discontinued', 'no regulatory filing'.

guideline_status.description: Guideline coverage: NCCN category, ESMO recommendation level, ASCO endorsement, etc. Free text. e.g. 'NCCN category 1 for ES-SCLC 2L; off-guideline for osteosarcoma'.

trials.description: Active trial pathways the patient could pursue. One entry per relevant trial.

patient_eligible.description: Does this trial accept the patient's tumor type per published eligibility?

sites_url.description: URL on ClinicalTrials.gov for the trial's site list.

notes.description: Slot availability, geography, time-to-screen, anything else useful for the user's outreach call.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer / marketer / sponsor contact info for medical-information inquiries, off-label requests, and compassionate-use requests.

compassionate_use_url.description: Direct URL for the manufacturer's compassionate-use / expanded-access portal when one exists.

payer_access_notes.description: Medicare/Medicaid coverage, NCD/LCD status, prior-authorization considerations, manufacturer patient-assistance programs. Free text.

access_summary.description: 2-3 sentence narrative summary the user can read in isolation. Names the realistic access path and the load-bearing constraint.

next_steps.description: Ordered list of concrete actions the user / treating team should take to pursue this pathway. e.g. 'Confirm DLL3 IHC SP347 result before enrollment', 'Email the NCT06788938 central contact to request screening slot'.

geographic_scope.description: Geographies where the access path is currently realistic. e.g. 'US + EU; mainland-China sites only', 'US sites only — not yet open in EU'.

last_verified_utc.description: ISO date the agent last verified this row in YYYY-MM-DD form. Information ages — record the verification date so a reviewer knows whether to re-screen.

notes.description: Caveats, recent news, sponsor-side updates that don't fit the structured fields.
